text.p: Spanish government bonds pulled back after a strong start to close broadly unchanged on Tuesday, and traders said the market was now focussing on a possible rate cut from the Bank of Spain on Friday.
"Bonos tracked bunds higher in early trade, but bunds met with resistance and the rally petered out," said one trader.
"The most important focus for bonos now is Friday's action from the central bank," he added.
Expectations for a rate cut are mixed, with some traders prepared for a cut in the key money rate on Friday and others expecting the Bank of Spain to hold off until later in December.

The yield spread against Germany made fresh lows in morning trade of 118 basis points compared with 124 basis points late on Monday. But by the close on Tuesday the spread had widened again to 122 bps.
